# `start_func`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Start the GoPixel function: centre the mount on a displayed-image pixel.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xdade0, StartCenterPixel @0x17da50 (64-bit build); app 3.3.2 BaseDeviceViewModel.startGoPixel, ModeRtspGoViewDelegate.startPreGo, ModeRtspViewModel.mapTouchToImagePoint |

Runs the general relay and mount-occupancy guard, converts the displayed pixel to a raw pixel through the video crop and ROI (the 32-bit build converts X and Y separately and has no conversion failure branch), then starts the centring worker asynchronously and returns at once with result 0. The guard may instead relay the request and return the peer reply. If x or y is malformed after an accepted name, the reply contains only the dispatcher metadata (no result and no error). While running, the centring function emits a function event carrying cur_pix, a two-integer array of the current raw pixel; its event name is not established from this handler and the request name GoPixel MUST NOT be assumed equal to it. The app 3.3.2 sends x and y as integer pixels of the unrotated wide-camera RTSP frame (origin top-left, x right, y down), scaled from the tap to the stream's native size (READ, app 3.3.2), and never sends stop_func GoPixel (READ, bounded search).

Side effects: Stores the target pixel and starts centring work that moves the mount; refuses a concurrent centring thread.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"start_func"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | yes | - | Object params are required; no positional form. Only the GoPixel function is accepted. [READ] |
| `params.name` | string | yes | - | Function to start. MUST be exactly GoPixel (case-sensitive); any other value, a missing or non-string name, null or non-object params is rejected with 100. Fixed value `"GoPixel"`. [READ] |
| `params.x` | integer | if name is GoPixel | - | Target X in displayed-image pixel coordinates (INFERRED from conversion helper names). Required for GoPixel; no range bound. A float, bool, string, null or missing value makes the handler return without writing a result or an error. [INFERRED] |
| `params.y` | integer | if name is GoPixel | - | Target Y in displayed-image pixel coordinates; same rules as x. [INFERRED] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 100 | params not an object, name missing, not a string, or not GoPixel | `invalid request` |
| 203 | Guard: local or remote mount is occupied | `equipment is moving` |
| 209 | Pixel conversion found invalid crop or show dimensions; or the selected camera is not the one required | `invalid value` |
| 268 | A centring thread is already running | `operation is in progress` |
| 212 | Worker thread could not be created | `fail to create thread` |
| 300 | Relay: main-process user context is null | `internal error` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Also listed in the evidence: 524 (function conflict) belongs to the guard variant used by other methods; the occupancy variant used here does not reach it. On a conversion or start failure the handler serializes the current thread error code without setting one itself; failures that set no code (lower crop calculation) give an unresolved code.

## Example

Request, go-pixel - Values invented:

```json
{"id":61,"method":"start_func","params":{"name":"GoPixel","x":540,"y":960}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_func","result":0,"code":0,"id":61}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_func","error":"equipment is moving","code":203,"id":62}
```
